## Start here


| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [`corehpc_nextflow_template.config`](https://github.com/gladstone-institutes/Bioinformatics-Workshops/blob/master/intro-to-corehpc/materials/nextflow/corehpc_nextflow_template.config) | SLURM executor, resource caps, containers, reports |
| [`launch_corehpc_template.sh`](https://github.com/gladstone-institutes/Bioinformatics-Workshops/blob/master/intro-to-corehpc/materials/nextflow/launch_corehpc_template.sh) | Submits Nextflow as a driver job; has a built-in smoke test |

Copy both, set `COREHPC_PROJECT`, and only edit when you need to adjust the resource requests or add rule specific behavior.

```bash
export COREHPC_PROJECT=/mnt/gladstone/<pi>/<share>/<project>
./launch_corehpc_template.sh smoke
```

::: {.callout-note}
Scratch is `/mnt/scratch` on both halves. Persistent storage differs: these
examples use Gladstone's `/mnt/gladstone`, so on the UCSF half substitute your
FAC share.
:::


## Step 1: Install Nextflow

Do this once **on the login node**, which is the only node with internet.
Nextflow needs Java, so install that first.

```bash
# Java, via SDKMAN
curl -s "https://get.sdkman.io" | bash
source ~/.sdkman/bin/sdkman-init.sh
sdk install java 17.0.6-tem

# Nextflow itself
mkdir -p ~/bin && cd ~/bin
wget -qO- https://get.nextflow.io | bash
export PATH=$HOME/bin:$PATH        # add this line to ~/.bashrc
nextflow -v
```


## Step 2: Install the nf-core tools

`nf-core` is a **Python package**, separate from the Nextflow engine. You need it
to download a pipeline for offline use, so install it into a conda environment:

```bash
module load miniforge3
conda create -n nf-core -c bioconda -c conda-forge nf-core
conda activate nf-core
nf-core --version
```

::: {.callout-tip}
Keep this environment small and only for the nf-core CLI. The pipeline's own
software comes from containers, not from this environment.
:::

## Step 3: Pre-fetch everything (login node only)

Compute nodes have **no internet**. Three separate things try to phone home, and
each needs its own fix.

```bash
export COREHPC_PROJECT=/mnt/gladstone/<pi>/<share>/<project>
export NXF_SINGULARITY_CACHEDIR=$COREHPC_PROJECT/singularity-cache

# 1 + 2. Pipeline code and its container images
nf-core pipelines download rnaseq \
  --revision 3.26.0 \
  --container-system singularity \
  --container-cache-utilisation amend \
  --compress none \
  --outdir $COREHPC_PROJECT/assets/nf-core-rnaseq-3.26.0

# 3. Plugins the pipeline pins, into the shared home
nextflow plugin install nf-schema@2.5.1
ls ~/.nextflow/plugins | grep nf-schema
```

**a) The pipeline itself.** `nextflow run nf-core/rnaseq -r 3.26.0` treats that as
a remote project and tries to pull it, giving
`Cannot read project manifest -- Cause: No route to host`. Run the **local** copy
produced by the download, with no `-r`.

**b) Self-update and remote configs.** Set `export NXF_OFFLINE=true` in the job
body. This disables the version check and the remote `nf-core/configs` fetch, and
forces cached plugins and images only.

**c) Plugins.** `NXF_OFFLINE=true` also means Nextflow will not download the
plugins the pipeline pins, so it fails with `Plugin with id nf-schema not found in
any repository`. Pre-fetch them as above.

::: {.callout-important}
The non-obvious flag is `--container-cache-utilisation amend`. It puts images into
`$NXF_SINGULARITY_CACHEDIR`, which **must equal** `singularity.cacheDir` in your
config so the offline run finds them. Confirm with `ls $NXF_SINGULARITY_CACHEDIR`
and expect `.img` or `.sif` files.
:::

Plugin versions change per release. Check the pipeline's own `nextflow.config`
`plugins { }` block for what your revision pins, rather than copying the version
above.

## Step 4: The config file

Copy `corehpc_nextflow_template.config` rather than writing this from scratch. It
reads every path from the environment, so the only thing you must set is
`COREHPC_PROJECT`. Optional overrides: `COREHPC_ACCOUNT`, `COREHPC_PARTITION`,
`COREHPC_SCRATCH`, `COREHPC_WORKDIR`, `COREHPC_CACHEDIR`, `COREHPC_REPORTS`.

The parts that matter on CoreHPC:

```groovy
process {
    executor       = 'slurm'
    queue          = partition                    // COREHPC_PARTITION, default 'cpu'
    clusterOptions = "--account=${account}"       // COREHPC_ACCOUNT, default 'hpc_core'

    // Replaces the removed --max_cpus/--max_memory/--max_time params.
    resourceLimits = [ cpus: 4, memory: 60.GB, time: 50.h ]

    // Drop -C (noclobber) from nf-core's default shell. See below.
    shell = ['bash', '-e', '-u', '-o', 'pipefail']

    // 137 = OOM, 140 = walltime, 143 = SIGTERM from the scheduler.
    errorStrategy = { task.exitStatus in [104,134,137,139,140,143,247] ? 'retry' : 'finish' }
    maxRetries    = 2
}

singularity {
    enabled    = true
    autoMounts = true
    cacheDir   = cachePath
    runOptions = "--bind ${scratch} --bind ${projRoot}"
}

executor {
    queueSize       = 20        // cap concurrent child jobs
    submitRateLimit = '10 sec'
    exitReadTimeout = '15 min'  // tolerate slow shared-FS exit-file visibility
}

report   { enabled = true; overwrite = true; file = 'reports/execution_report.html' }
timeline { enabled = true; overwrite = true; file = 'reports/execution_timeline.html' }
trace    { enabled = true; overwrite = true; file = 'reports/execution_trace.txt' }
```

### `resourceLimits`, not `--max_cpus`

Recent nf-core pipelines removed `--max_cpus` / `--max_memory` / `--max_time`. Any
request above `resourceLimits` is clamped down instead. A launch command still
carrying `--max_*` flags will error.

### noclobber breaks `-resume`

nf-core's default process shell includes `-C` (noclobber). On `-resume` after an
interrupted or requeued run, a task reruns in its **old** work directory where its
output file still exists, and `-C` makes the `>` redirect fail with
`cannot overwrite existing file`. Drop `-C`, keep `-euo pipefail`.

### `overwrite = true` on reports

Without it, a relaunch aborts immediately with
`Trace file already exists ... enable the 'trace.overwrite' option`. Each relaunch
then replaces the previous run's report files, so copy them aside to keep them.

### Bind mounts

Set both the config `runOptions --bind` and `APPTAINER_BINDPATH` in the job body,
covering scratch and the project root. Containers cannot see paths that are not
bound, and the resulting error usually reads as a missing input file.

### Per-process overrides

Start from the defaults and override only what actually failed:

```groovy
withName: 'STAR_GENOMEGENERATE' { cpus = 4; memory = '60.GB'; time = '8.h' }
withName: 'STAR_ALIGN'          { cpus = 4; memory = '40.GB'; time = '8.h' }

// Loads the decoy-aware index; 16 GB OOM'd (exit 137). Scale on retry.
withName: 'SALMON_QUANT'        { cpus = 4; memory = { 24.GB * task.attempt }; time = '4.h' }

// Fails on upstream fastq md5 mismatches that do not affect alignment.
withName: 'FQ_LINT'             { errorStrategy = 'ignore' }
```

Exit status 137 is always OOM. Prefer `{ N.GB * task.attempt }` over a single large
fixed request, so the first attempt stays schedulable.

## Step 5: Run it as a driver job

Because the login node reaps processes on disconnect, you cannot just run
`nextflow run ...` in your SSH session. **Submit Nextflow itself as a SLURM job.**
That driver job sits on a compute node orchestrating, and submits one child SLURM
job per pipeline task via the `slurm` executor.

The driver is cheap: 1 CPU, 8 GB, it only polls. Give it a long walltime
(`sinfo -o "%P %l"` shows the partition cap).

::: {.callout-warning}
## The walltime cap differs by half

The 5-day `--time` below is a **Gladstone-half** value. On the **UCSF half** jobs
are capped at **48 hours**, so that request is rejected outright and a long
pipeline will not fit in a single driver job.

On the UCSF half, treat [Step 6](#step-6-surviving-the-driver-walltime) as
mandatory rather than a nicety: set `--time=48:00:00`, keep the requeue trap, and
expect the driver to checkpoint and restart at least once on a large run. Confirm
your own cap with `sinfo -o "%P %l"` before setting `DRIVER_TIME`.
:::

```bash
sbatch --parsable \
  --job-name="rnaseq_driver" \
  --account=hpc_core --partition=cpu \
  --time=5-00:00:00 --mem=8G --cpus-per-task=1 \
  --requeue --signal=B:TERM@300 --open-mode=append \
  --chdir="$SCRIPT_DIR" --output="$LOG" \
  "$JOBSCRIPT"
```

Inside the job script:

```bash
export NXF_OFFLINE=true
export NXF_SINGULARITY_CACHEDIR=$COREHPC_PROJECT/singularity-cache
export APPTAINER_BINDPATH="/mnt/scratch,$COREHPC_PROJECT"

nextflow run $COREHPC_PROJECT/assets/nf-core-rnaseq-3.26.0/3_26_0 \
  -profile singularity -c corehpc.config -resume \
  --input samplesheet.csv \
  --outdir $COREHPC_PROJECT/results
```

Write the job body to an inspectable `.sbatch` file rather than piping to `sbatch`
on stdin. `launch_corehpc_template.sh check` writes and prints it without
submitting, which is the fastest way to catch a bad path or an empty argument
before burning a queue slot. Printing the Nextflow argv from inside the job turns
"mysterious Nextflow arg error" into "there is an empty string in position 7":

```bash
echo "nextflow argv:"; printf '  <%s>\n' "${NF[@]}"
```

### Driver memory and the JVM heap

The launcher sets `NXF_OPTS` in the job body:

```bash
export NXF_OPTS='-Xms1g -Xmx6g'      # derived from DRIVER_MEM
```

This is not optional tuning. The JVM sizes its default maximum heap from the RAM
it believes the machine has, and under SLURM it generally sees the **whole
node**, not your cgroup limit. On a large compute node that default ceiling is
tens of GB, so the driver's heap can grow past `--mem`, SLURM's cgroup kills it,
and you get **exit 137 on the driver itself**. That reads as a mysterious mid-run
crash rather than a memory setting.

`-Xmx` must therefore stay below `--mem`, with room for the JVM's non-heap
footprint (metaspace, thread stacks, GC structures, code cache). The launcher
derives it as 75% of `DRIVER_MEM` so the two cannot drift apart:

| `DRIVER_MEM` | JVM heap |
|---|---|
| `4G` | `3g` |
| `8G` (default) | `6g` |
| `16G` | `12g` |

Override it directly with `NXF_HEAP` if you need to. `-Xms` only avoids GC churn
while the first few hundred tasks are submitted, and is not load-bearing.

### If the cluster ever permits lingering

If `loginctl enable-linger $USER` is ever allowed, running the orchestrator in
`tmux` on the login node is simpler, and then only the short-lived child jobs have
walltimes. It was not permitted for us.

## Step 6: Surviving the driver walltime

The driver is a job, so it has a walltime, and a big run can outlast it. The
launcher checkpoints and requeues itself:

- `--signal=B:TERM@300` makes SLURM send `SIGTERM` to the driver 300 s before the
  walltime.
- A trap stops Nextflow gracefully. Nextflow flushes the `-resume` cache and
  cancels its running child jobs.
- `scontrol requeue $SLURM_JOB_ID` restarts the same job, `--requeue` and
  `--open-mode=append` let it resume into the same log, and `-resume` picks up from
  the cache.

```bash
NF_PID=""
on_term() {
  echo "[driver] TERM near walltime -- graceful stop + requeue $(date)"
  kill -TERM "$NF_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
  wait "$NF_PID" 2>/dev/null
  scontrol requeue "$SLURM_JOB_ID" || echo "[driver] requeue failed"
  exit 0
}
trap on_term TERM

"${NF[@]}" &          # background so the trap can fire
NF_PID=$!
wait "$NF_PID"
```

**What survives:** every task that completed and was cached.
**What does not:** tasks mid-flight at the cutoff get recomputed. Nextflow cannot
pause a running task or re-attach to an orphaned child job.

Set `DRIVER_TIME` as high as the partition allows to minimize restarts. On the
UCSF half that ceiling is 48 hours, so restarts are expected on a large run and
this section is the difference between a pipeline that finishes and one that
silently loses two days of work.
`SIGNAL_GRACE` only needs to cover Nextflow's own shutdown (seconds), not the
running tasks. If the cluster disallows requeue or in-job `scontrol`, the trap logs
a failure and the job ends; just relaunch manually, `-resume` still works.

::: {.callout-tip}
Always run with `-resume`. It costs nothing on a fresh run and saves days on a
restart.
:::

## Verifying the setup

Do not debug your cluster setup and your pipeline at the same time. Run the smoke
test first:

```bash
export COREHPC_PROJECT=/mnt/gladstone/<pi>/<share>/<project>
./launch_corehpc_template.sh smoke check   # inspect the sbatch, submit nothing
./launch_corehpc_template.sh smoke         # submit it
```

It writes a three-task pipeline into `$COREHPC_PROJECT/corehpc_smoke_test/` and runs
it through the same driver job, config and SLURM executor a real run uses. It takes
a couple of minutes. Then:

```bash
cat $COREHPC_PROJECT/corehpc_smoke_test/results/smoke_report.txt
```

Every task should report a real SLURM job id, the cpus and memory your config
granted it, and a work directory under `$COREHPC_PROJECT`. That confirms the
scheduler, account, partition, config and work directory are all wired up. If the
container cache already holds an image, the report also confirms Singularity runs
and that the project bind mount is visible from inside the container.

Now run it a **second** time. Every task should say `CACHED`, which is what proves
`-resume` works. Without that, a requeue after the driver walltime will recompute
everything. Delete `$COREHPC_PROJECT/corehpc_smoke_test/` when you are done.

### Pre-flight checklist

Once the smoke test passes, run this before each new pipeline:

```bash
which nextflow; nextflow -version                   # engine present
which singularity || which apptainer                # if only apptainer, use -profile apptainer
ls ~/.nextflow/plugins                              # pinned plugins pre-fetched
ls $NXF_SINGULARITY_CACHEDIR                        # images present (.img/.sif)
ls $PIPELINE/main.nf                                # local pipeline copy exists
ls $SAMPLESHEET                                     # and every path inside it
sinfo -o "%P %l"                                    # partition walltime cap vs DRIVER_TIME
sacctmgr show assoc user=$USER format=account,partition   # account is valid
```

Then run `./launch_corehpc_template.sh check`, read the printed sbatch, and submit.
Watch it with `squeue -u $USER` (driver first, then child `nf-*` jobs) and
`tail -f <driver log>`.

## Samplesheet gotcha: sample IDs must not be bare numbers

Sample IDs like `4107` are parsed by nf-schema as integers and fail the
samplesheet's `type: string` check. Prefix them (`TH_4107`). This also keeps R from
mangling counts-matrix column names later.

## Getting results back

Transfer through **`gsdt02.gladstone.internal`**, not a CoreHPC login node, and
remember the mount point changes to `/gladstone/...` there.

Pull only the small outputs. Alignments, fastqs, bigwigs and the on-the-fly
STAR/RSEM/salmon index are tens to hundreds of GB and belong on the cluster.

Note that the Nextflow `report` / `timeline` / `trace` files land next to the
launcher (per the `file =` paths in the config), **not** in `--outdir`, so they need
a second transfer.

## Error quick reference

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `Cannot read project manifest -- No route to host` | Compute node pulling the pipeline from GitHub | Run the local downloaded copy, no `-r`; `NXF_OFFLINE=true` |
| `Plugin with id nf-schema not found in any repository` | Offline mode cannot download plugins | `nextflow plugin install nf-schema@<version>` on the login node |
| Run dies when SSH disconnects | Login node reaps user processes | Submit Nextflow as a driver job |
| `cannot overwrite existing file` on `-resume` | nf-core default shell includes `-C` (noclobber) | `shell = ['bash','-e','-u','-o','pipefail']` |
| `Trace file already exists` | Report files from the previous run | `overwrite = true` in `report` / `timeline` / `trace` |
| Exit status 137 | OOM | Raise memory, ideally `{ N.GB * task.attempt }` |
| `--max_cpus` unrecognized | Params removed from recent nf-core | `resourceLimits = [...]` in the config |
| Samplesheet schema error on a sample ID | Bare-numeric ID read as an integer | Prefix the ID (`TH_4107`) |
| Input file "not found" inside a container | Path not bound | Add to `runOptions --bind` and `APPTAINER_BINDPATH` |
| Job dies at driver walltime | Run outlasted `DRIVER_TIME` | Requeue trap above, and relaunch with `-resume` |
